title: Proper geometric-fibre formula and exchange on vanishing topoi
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be morphisms of schemes, with $h$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and put $f=gh$. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $m\geq1$. Use the vanishing topoi, their projections $p_{f,1}:V_f\to X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $p_{g,1}:V_g\to Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and the induced morphism $\bar h:V_f\to V_g$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Work in the bounded-below derived categories of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves of that definition. For a geometric point $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ [def-weil-geometric-point], a geometric point $t$ of $S$, and a specialization $c:t\to g(y)$ (a morphism of strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]), let $z=(y,t,c)$ be the associated point of $V_g$. Put $X_y=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The universal property in [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] gives $\phi_z:(X_y)_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$ from $X_y\to X$, the constant geometric point $t$, and $c$; on points it sends $x$ to $(x,t,c)$. For every $A\in D^+(V_f,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$z^*R\bar h_*A\simeq R\Gamma((X_y)_{\mathrm{Et}},\phi_z^*A),$$
induced by restriction to the proper geometric fibre, compatibly with the direct-image counits. Here $R\Gamma$ is derived global sections, computed by the K-injective resolutions used in [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].
For any scheme morphism $T\to S$, put $X_T=X\times_ST$, $Y_T=Y\times_ST$, $f_T:X_T\to T$, $g_T:Y_T\to T$ and $h_T:X_T\to Y_T$, and let $v_f:V_{f_T}\to V_f$, $v_g:V_{g_T}\to V_g$ be the induced morphisms. The canonical adjunction-defined comparison is an isomorphism
$$v_g^*R\bar h_*A\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar h_{T,*}v_f^*A.$$
For every $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ the first-projection comparison is likewise an isomorphism
$$p_{g,1}^*Rh_*B\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar h_*p_{f,1}^*B.$$
No constructibility, Noetherian, finite-dimensional, or finite-Tor assumption is made.

proof.text: Construct $\phi_z$ by the universal property: its first component is $i:X_y\to X$, its second is the constant point $t$, and its orientation is the pullback of $c$ along $X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Its composite with $\bar h$ is $z$ followed by the global-sections morphism of $X_y$. In particular $p_{f,1}\phi_z=i$. Define the restriction map $\theta_z:z^*R\bar h_*A\to R\Gamma(X_y,\phi_z^*A)$ to be the mate of this equality of inverse images. In the adjunctions of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], its adjunct is $\phi_z^*\bar h^*R\bar h_*A\xrightarrow{\phi_z^*\varepsilon_{\bar h}}\phi_z^*A$. This specifies the actual map, including its counit normalization.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 9.1.1, proof, printed pp. 19–20; ILO XI 2.3 and 2.7, printed pp. 178–181

proof.text: Let $I$ be the small cofiltered category of affine pointed triples at $z$ of [lem-trf-oriented-affine-neighbourhood-limit], with $s=g(y)$. We show that its three component functors, to the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods of $y$ in $Y$, of $s$ in $S$ and of $t$ in $S$, are initial, so that [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] gives $\varprojlim_IU=Y_{(y)}$, $\varprojlim_IV=S_{(s)}$, $\varprojlim_IW=S_{(t)}$. By the inverse-image formula of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal], a point of $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ at $z$ is a lift of $y$ to $U$ and a lift of $t$ to $W$ whose images in $V$ are related by $c$. Nonempty comma categories: given an affine pointed neighbourhood $U_0$ of $y$ (resp. $V_0$ of $s$, $W_0$ of $t$), take an affine pointed neighbourhood $V$ of $s$ (inside $V_0$ in the second case), an affine open $U$ of $U_0\times_SV$ (in the other two cases, of $Y\times_SV$) containing the lift of $y$, and an affine open $W$ of $W_0\times_SV$ (in the other two cases, of $V$) containing the lift of $t$ through $S_{(t)}\xrightarrow{c}S_{(s)}\to V$; this pointed triple maps to the given neighbourhood. Connected comma categories: two such arrows are first dominated by one object of $I$, as $I$ is cofiltered; the two resulting pointed maps to $U_0$ (resp. $V_0$, $W_0$) are equalized by a pointed neighbourhood [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered]; shrink it to an affine open containing the point and, in the middle case, pull the other two components back to it and shrink them likewise. This gives an object of $I$ connecting the two. The arrow $\varprojlim W\to\varprojlim V$ is $c$ by the compatibility clause of [lem-trf-oriented-affine-neighbourhood-limit], and $\varprojlim_I(X\times_YU)=X\times_YY_{(y)}=X^\ell$ since fibre products commute with limits.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 9.1.1, proof, printed pp. 19–20; ILO XI 2.3 and 2.7, printed pp. 178–181

proof.text:
Put $s=g(y)$, $Y^\ell=Y_{(y)}$, $S^\ell=S_{(s)}$, $S^t=S_{(t)}$, and $X^\ell=X\times_Y Y^\ell$. The specialization gives $S^t\to S^\ell$. Let $Q=(X^\ell)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(S^\ell)_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S^t)_{\mathrm{Et}}$, with restriction $A^\ell$. Take the small initial cofiltered system of affine pointed triples $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ at $z$ given by [lem-trf-oriented-affine-neighbourhood-limit]. Their inverse images under $\bar h$ are the sheafified triples $(X\times_YU\to V\leftarrow W)$, by the universal inverse-image formula. Their slices are the corresponding oriented products by [lem-trf-oriented-slice-localization]. Each $X\times_YU$ is proper over affine $U$, hence qcqs; its arrow to affine $V$ is qcqs. Transitions in all three components are affine: in the first they are base changes of maps between affine $U$'s. Thus [lem-trf-oriented-derived-cohomology-continuity] applies after fixing one triple and restricting to its cofiltered refinement category. The component limits are $X^\ell,S^\ell,S^t$ by the preceding step. The exact stalk colimit [lem-trf-site-point-fibre], applied to a K-injective representative, now gives
$$z^*R\bar h_*A\simeq R\Gamma(Q,A^\ell).$$
Indeed, for a K-injective $J$ representing $A$ and a triple $T$ with inverse image $T'$, $(\bar h_*J)(T)=J(T')=\operatorname{Hom}(H_{T'},J)=\Gamma(V_f/H_{T'},j^*J)$; restriction $j^*$ to the slice is exact with exact left adjoint $j_!$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction], so a chain map from an acyclic $N$ to $j^*J$ is adjoint to one from the acyclic $j_!N$ to $J$, hence null-homotopic: $j^*J$ is K-injective and computes $R\Gamma$ of the slice. The composition normalization and continuity give the displayed isomorphism as restriction, not an arbitrary isomorphism of cohomology groups.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 9.1.1, proof, printed pp. 19–20; ILO XI 2.3 and 2.7, printed pp. 178–181

proof.text:
Let $\pi:Q\to(X^\ell)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ be the first projection and $i_y:X_y\to X^\ell$ the geometric-fibre map. We show that the restriction comparison $i_y^*R\pi_*A^\ell\to\phi_z^*A$ is an isomorphism. At a geometric point $x$ of $X_y$, compute the stalk of $R\pi_*A^\ell$ by affine etale neighbourhoods $U$ of its image in $X^\ell$. Localization of the oriented product identifies the inverse-image slices with $U_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(S^\ell)_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S^t)_{\mathrm{Et}}$. The exact stalk-colimit formula, K-injectivity of slice restrictions of a K-injective representative (as in the previous step, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]), and continuity identify the stalk complex with
$$R\Gamma((X^\ell)_{(x),\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{(S^\ell)_{\mathrm{Et}}}(S^t)_{\mathrm{Et}},A^\ell|).$$
All schemes and arrows here are qcqs: restrict $U$ inside an affine neighbourhood, and keep $S^\ell,S^t$ fixed and affine. Their transition maps are affine. The map $(X^\ell)_{(x)}\to S^\ell$ is local between strictly henselian local schemes, since $x$ lies over the closed point $s$. Apply [lem-trf-local-oriented-projection-exact] to its second projection. Its direct image is the exact inverse image by the canonical section. Global sections on $S^t$ are its closed-point stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk]; [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] carries this identity to constant modules. Consequently the displayed complex is exactly $A_{(x,t,c)}$, and the comparison is the germ restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-stalk-conservative] to the underlying abelian complexes; forgetting scalar actions reflects zero kernels and cokernels, so this detects the isomorphism on $X_y$. Notice that $i_y$ need not be a closed immersion if $\Omega$ extends the strict-local residue field; this argument uses the geometric-fibre map itself.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 9.1.1, proof, printed pp. 19–20; ILO XI 2.3 and 2.7, printed pp. 178–181

proof.text:
Let $h^\ell:X^\ell\to Y^\ell$ be the base change of $h$. It is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Put $C=R\pi_*A^\ell\in D^+(X^\ell,\Lambda)$. Every cohomology sheaf of its underlying abelian complex is killed by $m$, since these are $\Lambda$-module sheaves and $m\Lambda=0$. Thus ordinary module proper base change [det-properbasechange-modules] applies to $h^\ell$ and the geometric point $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y^\ell$. Using exact sections equal to the closed-point stalk on the strictly henselian $Y^\ell$, it gives
$$R\Gamma(X^\ell,C)\simeq R\Gamma(X_y,i_y^*C).$$
The sections/stalk equality for modules follows from the abelian equality and [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget]. Compose with the isomorphism of Step 4 and with $R\Gamma(Q,A^\ell)\simeq R\Gamma(X^\ell,R\pi_*A^\ell)$. The latter is the derived composition comparison for right adjoints to exact inverse images. With Step 3 this proves that $\theta_z$ is invertible. By mate pasting, all these restriction maps compose to the mate defined in Step 1; hence the result is natural and has the asserted compatibility with direct-image counits.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 9.1.1, proof, printed pp. 19–20; ILO XI 2.3 and 2.7, printed pp. 178–181

proof.text: Fix $T\to S$ and a point $z'=(y',t',c')$ of $V_{g_T}$, with $y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y_T$. Choose its image point $z$ on $V_g$ using the same field $\Omega$ for the composite $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$. The scheme fibres $(X_T)_{y'}$ and $X_y$ are canonically identical: specifying an $X_T$-point over $y'$ specifies an $X$-point over $y$, the $T$-coordinate already being fixed by $y'$. The universal property gives $v_f\phi_{z'}\simeq\phi_z$ on this common fibre; its orientation is the image of $c'$. Steps 1–5 apply also to $h_T$, which is proper by base change. Pull back the specified base-change comparison along $z'$. Mate pasting identifies the resulting arrow, under the two fibre formulas, with the identity restriction of $R\Gamma(X_y,\phi_z^*A)$, since the square just described is the identity on its fibre and coefficients. Therefore every oriented-point inverse image of this comparison is invertible. The conservativity theorem proves the base-change clause. No extension-of-algebraically-closed-fields theorem is needed: the source and target formulas use the same chosen $\Omega$.

source.place: Orgogozo, Lemma 9.1.1, proof, printed pp. 19–20; ILO XI 2.3 and 2.7, printed pp. 178–181

proof.text: For $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ apply ordinary module proper base change [det-properbasechange-modules] at $y$ to $h$ and $B$. Its torsion hypothesis holds because $m\Lambda=0$. At $z=(y,t,c)$ it identifies the source of the first-projection comparison with $R\Gamma(X_y,i^*B)$. Steps 1–5 identify its target with $R\Gamma(X_y,\phi_z^*p_{f,1}^*B)$. The equality $p_{f,1}\phi_z=i$ makes these coefficient complexes equal by composition of exact inverse images. Both maps to this fibre complex are adjoint to the pulled-back direct-image counit: mate pasting therefore makes the stalk of the specified first-projection comparison the identity under these identifications. Conservativity of the oriented points proves that comparison invertible. The arguments use only bounded-below complexes, properness, and the torsion supplied by $m\Lambda=0$; there is no constructibility or Tor-dimension input.

lean.statement: theorem properFibreExchange {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [IsProper h] (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ] (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hΛ : (m : Λ) = 0) : (∀ (Ω Ξ : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] [Field Ξ] [IsAlgClosed Ξ] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (t : Spec (.of Ξ) ⟶ S) (c : Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme t ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme (y ≫ g)) (hc : c ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap (y ≫ g) = Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap t) (A : VanishingDerived (h ≫ g) Λ), IsBoundedBelow (vanishingDatum.{u, v} (h ≫ g)) (Coeff.{u, v} Λ) A → IsIso ((fibreExchange.{u, v} h g y t c hc Λ).app A) ∧ (((globalModules.{u, v} h y).adj (Coeff.{u, v} Λ)).homEquiv _ _).symm ((fibreExchange.{u, v} h g y t c hc Λ).app A) = fibreCounit.{u, v} h g y t c hc Λ A) ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (q : T ⟶ S) (A : VanishingDerived (h ≫ g) Λ), IsBoundedBelow (vanishingDatum.{u, v} (h ≫ g)) (Coeff.{u, v} Λ) A → IsIso ((baseExchange.{u, v} h g q Λ).app A)) ∧ (∀ B : EtaleDerived X Λ, IsBoundedBelow (etaleDatum.{u, v} X) (Coeff.{u, v} Λ) B → IsIso ((firstExchange.{u, v} h g Λ).app B))
